chunks: What the Sheikh (may Allah the Exalted support him) informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from al-Husayn, from some of his companions, from Misma', from Abi Abdillah (AS):
He said: the Commander of the Faithful (AS) said: "It has been forbidden for a man to urinate in flowing water except out of necessity." And he said: "Truly, water has its own inhabitants."
Then he said: "It is not permissible for anyone to face the two discs of the sun and the moon with his private parts during urination or defecation."
And what indicates [the correctness of] this [ruling follows]...

key_terms.أَهْلًا: inhabitants, folk (spiritual beings — understood in the tradition as jinn — dwelling in water)
key_terms.الْجَارِي: flowing, running (qualifying water as moving — a key jurisprudential distinction for tahara)
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: necessity, exigent circumstance (the recognized fiqh principle permitting otherwise prohibited acts under compulsion)
key_terms.غَائِطٍ: defecation (classical Arabic euphemism, lit. 'low ground', referring to the secluded spot used for relieving oneself)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia Islamic ruling on urinating in flowing water, and is it forbidden to face the sun or moon with one's private parts while relieving oneself?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) on the authority of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), establishes two jurisprudential rulings on conduct during elimination: urinating in flowing water is prohibited except under necessity, since water possesses spiritual inhabitants; and it is impermissible for anyone to face the sun or moon with their private parts during urination or defecation. The closing phrase 'and what indicates this' is an editorial notation by al-Tusi signalling that further corroborating textual evidence follows within the chapter.
